metadata.summary: Mercedes' George Russell is set to take another grid penalty in November's Las Vegas Grand Prix.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver planning to take another grid penalty for upgraded power unit element at Las Vegas Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver planning to take another grid penalty for upgraded power unit element at Las Vegas Grand Prix George Russell has revealed he plans to take a grid penalty at next month's Las Vegas Grand Prix to allow an upgraded power unit element to be fitted to his car; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 13 October 2026 10:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle and Kim Kardashian put their awkward Monaco exchange behind them with a Singapore grid walk interview Mercedes' George Russell is set to take another grid penalty in November's Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell started at the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change following an engine issue at the previous race in Malaysia which saw him retire late on. He recovered to ninth but now trails Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli by 102 points in the Drivers' Championship with six rounds remaining, so is all but mathematically out of the title fight. messages.text: 'State of the Game' report finds most English clubs living on financial brink

metadata.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
metadata.content: 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink The Independent Football Regulator published its draft ‘State of the Game’ report on Tuesday, which found that while English football generated £9bn in revenue last season, 94 per cent of clubs in the top five divisions were loss-making Geraint Hughes Sports News Correspondent Tuesday 13 October 2026 17:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter Geraint Hughes explains the Independent Football Regulator's 'State of the Game' report, which explores how most English clubs are living on the brink of financial ruin The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster. The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform.
